source_claims_used: GrIPS is a gradient-free edit-based instruction search method for improving task instructions.
The public method iteratively uses phrase-level delete, add, swap and paraphrase operations.
The official repository implements iterative search and exposes candidate/iteration/patience controls; model execution can require GPU or external API access.
Published benchmark gains are not reproduced or claimed by this controller audit.

chat_native_reduction.candidate_status: Every edited policy starts UNEVALUATED; edit operation or textual plausibility cannot create score or credit.
chat_native_reduction.selection: Greedy or bounded-beam retention is allowed only among safe independently evidenced candidates; exact value tie preserves incumbent.
chat_native_reduction.recovery: Durable pending switch and sealed factual selector decision override edit generation/reselection.

edit_counterexamples.invariant: Delete cannot remove or weaken frozen root/config/control binding.
Add cannot introduce forbidden O/other-worker/downstream/legacy semantic inputs.
Swap cannot reorder semantics so protected authority becomes executable before Chat-capable work.
Paraphrase cannot erase stable frontier/candidate/transition identity or exact acceptance boundary.
An edited candidate's own claim of improvement is not a score.
Safe edit remains UNEVALUATED until independent terminal evidence is durably read back.
Equivalent stable candidate identity is evaluated once.
A safe edit with independent terminal evidence and strictly better frozen mechanical value may replace incumbent.
Exact value tie keeps incumbent instead of gratuitous edit churn.

interpretation_guard: Constructed recurring-Chat controller conformance only. GrIPS benchmark performance is not reproduced. The transferred mechanism is bounded textual edit search; published observation that prompt edits can improve model accuracy does not permit edits to weaken CLEAN, safety, authority, identity or durability invariants.
